chapter: Childhood, first teachers and the Wilberforce Collegians
title: Making discs and studying them; campus popularity
summary: The band cut little wax discs, played them back and studied them in night classes more than their books, and were popular on campus.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: It would be great if you could.

It was really something. And from these greats -- these guys that we're talking about were creators of jazz, Tom, in those days. We didn't know that at that time, but they were the creators. They weren't imitators, see. So we got this first hand. We got this -- so we were just like going to school. Boy, when I come back to school in September, we'd hold night classes -- music classes on our own, and we'd try things out, and there was such things in those days as making, you know, little discs. They were 78's, you know --

-- wax, yeah. And I made quite a few of those. I brought them back because we'd play 'em back, you know, and let the guys hear 'em, and then we'd pick out a certain tune, and we'd just go to school on this thing. We spent more time on that than we did our books, our studies. I don't know how we ever graduated. But, let me say one thing. I'll tell you how we did. We were popular on the

campus, naturally, because we were a jolly bunch. All the girls liked the boys, naturally, and even the men liked the guys (unintelligible) as great musicians, the chefs that they had there, even the professors and everybody. I would say that they used to lean a little bit for us, because I'll tell you why. Can I give you one instance?
